message:
[XLA:GPU][NFC] Make the PriorityFusion decision chain non-blocking

`GetTiledRunTimeDataCached` blocks a thread pool worker in `Await()` while it
waits for the tiling search. That is safe only as long as the cost model
evaluates its candidates inline. Once the cost model is given the same thread
pool, the parked worker is waiting on tasks queued onto the pool whose slot it
occupies, and with a fan-out wider than the pool every worker parks at once.

This change converts the whole decision chain to continuation-passing style so
that no thread pool worker ever blocks:

```
GetTiledRunTimeDataCached           -> GetTiledRunTimeDataCachedAsync
CanFuseTriton                       -> CanFuseTritonAsync
CanFuse                             -> CanFuseAsync
CanFuseCached                       -> CanFuseCachedAsync
CanFuseWithAllNonBitcastUsers       -> CanFuseWithAllNonBitcastUsersAsync
FindPossibleConsumersForTriton...   -> ...Async
CalculateProducerPriority           -> CalculateProducerPriorityAsync
```

After this change `PriorityFusion` blocks in exactly two places,
`ComputePriorities` and `DequeueNextProducer`, and both run on the thread
driving `PriorityFusion::Run`, which holds no pool slot. `AwaitFusionDecision`
documents that contract for its two callers.

`ComputePriorities` keeps its fork/join shape. The scheduled closure now only
starts the computation and returns; the priority is written by a continuation
on whichever thread resolves the decision. The `absl::BlockingCounter` stays,
because blocking on the `Run` thread is not the problem and the counter also
preserves index-ordered error reporting for free.

Two shape decisions worth knowing when reviewing:

`GetTiledRunTimeDataCachedAsync` uses `OnReady`, not `Map`. Its contract is to
fold a failed status into a negative `FusionDecision`, so the continuation has
to observe the status, which `Map` does not expose. `Map` is also explicitly
permitted to skip a continuation whose result it believes is unused, which
would silently drop the cache write. The `HloFusionAdaptor` moves into the
continuation for the same reason the old code kept it on the stack: the cost
model captures it by reference and it has to outlive the returned future.

`CanFuseWithAllNonBitcastUsersAsync` walks the users through the iterative
`CheckUsersFrom` rather than recursing. An already-resolved decision runs its
continuation inline, so a recursive formulation would push a stack frame per
user; producers with a few thousand users do occur, and at roughly 640 bytes
per frame that overflows the 2 MiB worker stack. Consuming ready decisions in
a loop keeps that case at constant stack depth.

This is a no-op today: the cost model is still invoked with a null executor, so
every future it returns is already available and every continuation runs inline
on the calling thread, in the same order as before.

PR #49603: [ROCM] bug-fixing matmul plan cache behaviour

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49603

📝 Summary of Changes
Fixing gpublaslt matmul plan cache thrashing behaviour under certain circumstances

🎯 Justification
It could happen that two structurally equal GEMMS get different autotuner keys while sharing the same matmul plan.
In particular, this happened for these two dot ops:
```
.16  bf16[1,1,5120]    x bf16[5120,40,128]   lhs_contracting={2},   rhs_contracting={0}
.25  bf16[1,1,40,128]  x bf16[40,128,5120]   lhs_contracting={2,3}, rhs_contracting={0,1}
```
Different ranks and contracting-dim counts ⇒ different fusion bodies ⇒ different
fingerprints ⇒ two independent groups. But 40·128 = 5120, so once GemmRewriter
absorbs the reshapes into bitcasts both become
bf16[5120,5120] x bf16[5120,1] -> bf16[5120,1], {1}/{0} — one **CanonicalGemmHlo**.

Then, these two gemms can be autotuned to different algorithm indices, e.g.:
- one with **selected_algorithm=0**
- another with **selected_algorithm=N** (non-zero).

This leads to matmul plan cache thrashing since gpublaslt_matmul_thunk chooses max_algorithms=1 when selected_algorithm=0. This tiny optimization actually not worth it and can be dropped. Additionally, here we also relax caching requirement in gpu_blas_lt.cc to prevent such problems in the future.

author: kodlan
message:
PR #47649: [XLA:GPU] Keep scatter window writes coalesced in ScatterSimplifier and the transpose folding

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47649

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Two changes that together restore coalesced memory writes for scatters whose
update window dims come before the indexed dims (for example a vmapped
`segment_sum`, where the batch dim is a window dim and the segment ids index
the minor dim):

- `ScatterSimplifier` gets a `reorder_operand_dims_for_coalescing` option
  (enabled in the GPU pipelines only). When a scatter would write strided
  windows under the default layouts, the operand dims are permuted so that
  `scatter_dims_to_operand_dims` becomes the identity mapping and the writes
  become contiguous, with transposes around the scatter restoring the
  original order. This conditionally restores the canonicalization that
  087e1a5960 removed: scatters that are already coalesced keep the current
  no-transpose behavior, and so do variadic scatters, scatters with batching
  dims, and scatters whose written volume is small relative to the operand
  (where the transpose copies would cost more than the coalescing wins).
- `TryFoldTransposeIntoScatter` in the algebraic simplifier now checks the
  same profitability predicate and refuses folds that would make the written
  windows less contiguous. Without this, the fold both undoes the
  ScatterSimplifier rewrite above and defeats user-side workarounds (a
  restoring `.transpose()` gets folded back into the scatter, recreating the
  strided form). Folds that improve or preserve contiguity still fire.

The shared predicate `ScatterSimplifier::WriteRunLength` computes the length
of the contiguous run of operand elements each scatter index writes.

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #47203 (cross-post of jax-ml/jax#39959): `segment_sum` under `vmap`
regressed ~6x on the reporter's GPU between JAX 0.9.1 and 0.9.2, and its
`out_axes=1` workaround regressed further in 0.10.2. Root cause chain:

- Since 087e1a5960, nothing in the GPU pipeline re-orients a scatter whose
  window dims are major, so every scatter index writes a strided window
  (strided atomics). Isolated on an RTX 2070 with identical indices and
  updates, only the operand orientation differing: 5.11 ms coalesced vs
  91.62 ms strided (18x).
- Since 8a228780ee, the unconditional transpose fold recreates the strided
  form out of the coalesced-scatter-plus-transpose pattern, so no HLO-level
  workaround survives.

With this PR, the issue's repro compiles back to the coalesced scatter plus
one cheap restoring transpose: 85-90 ms -> ~5.5 ms on the RTX 2070 (~16x),
details in the Benchmark section.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement / 🐛 Bug Fix

## 📊 Benchmark

Issue repro as a standalone HLO (vmapped segment_sum: scatter-add of
f32[1024,75960] updates into 12123 segments, hashed pseudo-random segment
ids, `hlo_runner_main_gpu --num_repeats=10`, RTX 2070, sm_75):

- before: 85-90 ms per execution, compiled scatter `f32[1024,12123]{1,0}`
  (strided window writes)
- after: 5.4-5.6 ms per execution (~16x), compiled scatter
  `f32[12123,1024]{1,0}` (coalesced) plus a restoring transpose

Isolated scatter kernel with identical indices and updates, only the operand
orientation differing (via JAX on the same GPU): 5.11 ms coalesced vs
91.62 ms strided (18x). A standalone `[12123,1024] -> [1024,12123]`
transpose costs 0.32 ms, so the inserted transposes are ~2% of the win.

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

- `scatter_simplifier_test.cc`: `ReordersOperandDimsForCoalescing`,
  `ReordersOperandDimsWithInsertedWindowDims` (non-monotonic
  `scatter_dims_to_operand_dims`), `DoesNotReorderCoalescedScatter`,
  `DoesNotReorderVariadicScatter`, `DoesNotReorderWhenUpdatesAreSmall`,
  `DoesNotReorderOperandDimsByDefault`.
- `algebraic_simplifier_test.cc`: `FoldTransposeIntoScatter` now uses a
  profitable example (window dims move to minor);
  `DoNotFoldTransposeIntoScatterWhenWritesBecomeStrided` covers the refused
  direction.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

Verified on a single RTX 2070 (sm_75):

- `//xla/tests:scatter_test_nvgpu_any` (36 cases) and
  `//xla/tests:select_and_scatter_test_nvgpu_any` pass.
- `//xla/service/gpu:gpu_compiler_test_nvgpu_any` and the GPU scatter
  emitter lit tests (`add`, `sorted_indices`, `permuted_indices`,
  `permuted_sorted_indices`) pass.
- `run_hlo_module --platform=gpu --reference_platform=interpreter` on a
  small version of the repro: results match.

author: ezhulenev
message:
PR #49719: [tsl:concurrency] Deduplicate AsyncValue type ids by type name across DSOs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49719

`AsyncValue` assigns each payload type a 16-bit type id by appending to a process-global `TypeInfoTable` and caching the resulting index in `GetTypeId<T>()`'s function-local static. This is unsafe once XLA is split across dynamically-linked libraries: XLA is built with `-fvisibility=hidden`, which demotes the `GetTypeId<T>()` local static to a per-DSO local. A type registered in more than one DSO therefore appends to the shared table more than once and receives a different id in each
DSO, so `IsType<T>()`/`DynCast<T>()` on an `AsyncValue` that crosses a DSO boundary can silently return the wrong answer.

Make registration idempotent by type name: `CreateTypeInfoAndReturnTypeIdImpl` now keys a `name->id` map on `typeid(T).name()` and returns the existing id when the same type is registered again, instead of allocating a fresh
one. The map lives behind a const-init mutex in the single out-of-line definition of the registration function, so all DSOs that resolve that symbol share one id per type. No caller changes are required.

This mirrors MLIR's `TypeID`, whose fallback resolver (r`egisterImplicitTypeID(getTypeName<T>())`) already keys on the type name rather than on registration order, giving a process-stable identity that survives across DSO boundary.

PR #49300: [XLA:GPU] Inline scan computation to_apply calls

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49300

Scan rewrite lowering converts scan operations into call-based expressions. However, the GPU kernel emitter cannot compute indexing maps for Call operations, causing compilation failures for GPU kernels containing scan. Exact error:

```
E0000 00:00:1789415358.746826 1768463 indexing_analysis.cc:1748] ComputeOutputToInputIndexing is not implemented for opcode call
F0000 00:00:1789415358.746906 1768463 computation_partitioner.cc:269] Check failed: operand_maps.size() == 1 (0 vs. 1)
```

author: beckerhe
message:
Disable libnvjitlink disk caching via the -no-cache option.

Unless `-no-cache` is passed to `nvJitLinkCreate`, `libnvJitLink` loads `libcuda.so`, calls `cuInit(0)`, and uses the CUDA driver's internal export table during `nvJitLinkAddData` to read and write the driver's on-disk JIT cache (`~/.nv/ComputeCache`). Aside from being redundant with XLA's own compilation caching and unnecessarily initializing the CUDA driver during compilation, concurrent access to `~/.nv/ComputeCache` across parallel processes or threads can cause the driver's `AddToCache` or `Get_Cache_Entry` callbacks to fail with `CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN` (999), which `libnvJitLink` treats as a fatal `NVJITLINK_ERROR_INTERNAL` (`ERROR 999: AddToCache`) even when PTX compilation succeeded.

Pass `-no-cache` to `nvJitLinkCreate` in `CompileAndLinkUsingLibNvJitLink` and `GetLatestPtxIsaVersionForLibNvJitLink` in xla/stream_executor/cuda/nvjitlink.cc to disable the driver-level cache and work around these failures.

message:
Fix PjRt StreamExecutor execution to check BufferSequencingEvent error after waiting on stream.

In `PjRtStreamExecutorRawLoadedExecutable::Execute`, `BufferSequencingEvent::WaitForEventOnStream()` blocks until the definition event has completed or failed.

Previously, `ev->IsPredeterminedError()` was checked before `ev->WaitForEventOnStream()`. When an asynchronous host-to-device transfer (or any in-flight dependency) was still executing or pending, `ev->IsPredeterminedError()` returned false.

`ev->WaitForEventOnStream()` then blocked until the event completed with error. author: dsharletg
message:
[XLA:CPU] Add support for copy operations and degenerate layout dimensions in YNNPACK

Adds support for kCopy operations in YNNPACK fusion and relaxes layout checks to tolerate out-of-order dimensions when their extents are 1.

This addresses fusion breakages and performance regressions identified in https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/49131:
- When reduction pipelines use keepdims=True (e.g. pairwise reductions such as gravitational N-body or RBF kernels), layout assignment can insert reshapes and copies with layouts like f32[M, N, 1]{1,0,2}.
- Previously, IsLayoutSupportedByYnn rejected any layout whose minor_to_major was not strictly descending, even if the out-of-order dimensions had extent 1 (which does not affect physical element ordering).
- Furthermore, kCopy was unsupported in YNNPACK, causing LibraryRewriter to truncate fusions at copy boundaries and split the pipeline into multiple custom fusions, forcing large O(M*N) intermediate buffers to be materialized in memory.

Key changes:
1. IsLayoutSupportedByYnn: Ignores extent-1 dimensions when verifying descending layouts.
2. IsCopyOpSupportedByYnn: Validates copy operations whose non-degenerate dimensions have matching layout and extents.
3. ynn_matcher.h: Registers HloOpcode::kCopy in SupportedOps() and dispatches in IsOpSupported().
4. ynn_emitter.cc: Implements DefineCopyOp using ynn_define_copy and emits copy operations in YNN subgraphs.
5. ynn_fusion_test.cc: Adds unit tests for copy operations and degenerate layout copies across bf16, f32, and f64.

author: vishwakt
message:
Check the SplitV input size against Tlen, and drop the redundant loop

input_shape.dim_size(split_dim) was converted to Tlen implicitly, so
with int32 or int8 size_splits an input size above the maximum of Tlen
was truncated: int32 sizes [1, 2] matched an input of size 2**32 + 3,
and the split silently dropped the rest of the input. Check the size
in int64 before converting it.

Split sizes are now checked for being non-negative before they are
summed, and the -1 size is bounded by the input size, so the later loop
that checked every size again can no longer fail; remove it. Also build
the overflow error with errors::InvalidArgument, as the rest of the
file does.

The int32 case of testSizeSplitsOverflowRaises used an input larger
than INT32_MAX to reach the kernel in graph mode, which the new check
rejects first. Use a small input, where graph mode stops at the shape
function instead, and test the truncation separately.

author: akuegel
message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix out-of-bounds index handling in ScatterDeterminismExpander

Previously, `ScatterDeterminismExpander` only checked for out-of-bounds scatter
indices when updates were non-scalar. For scalar updates with multi-dimensional
scatter indices, `SortIndicesAndUpdates` flattened the indices via a dot product
with the operand strides without validating each component. Out-of-bounds
coordinates in one dimension (e.g., `(0, 4)` or `(1, -4)` on a `[2, 4]` operand)
could wrap into adjacent rows and overwrite valid elements instead of being
dropped.

Additionally, for non-scalar updates with implicit dimensions,
`out_of_bound_tensor` was padded with `0`s for implicit dimensions via
`AddImplicitDimensionsToIndices`. When `ExpandIndices` added non-zero window
offsets along an implicit dimension, the flattened out-of-bounds index could
collide with valid in-bounds indices.

Validate multi-dimensional scatter indices and mask out-of-bounds rows with
`out_of_bound_tensor` in the scalar-update path before sorting, and recreate
`out_of_bound_tensor` via `CreateBoundTensor` using the full index-to-operand
dimension mapping when implicit dimensions are added.

Fixes #49380

author: vishwakt
message:
Retrace tf.function for equal Python values of another type or sign

tf.function keys its trace cache on Python arguments through Literal,
which compared values with ==. Values that compare equal still trace
differently: 1, 1.0 and True give tensors of different dtypes, and
math.copysign or a division tells 0.0 and -0.0 apart. A call with one
of them reused the trace of another, so after f(1), f(1.0) returned an
int32 tensor, and after f(0.0), f(-0.0) returned the result for 0.0.

Make a Literal match only values of the same type and, for floats and
complex numbers, the same signs. NaNs still match each other. Literal
.cast, which checks the arguments of a concrete function call, uses the

author: jcai19
message:
[XLA][HLO Value Tracking] Maintain OriginalValue consistency in MemorySpaceAssignment

Root Cause:
`MemorySpaceAssignment::Process()` rewrites the HLO graph in two sequential loops over all `Allocation` objects:
1. Loop 1 calls the virtual method `Allocation::Process()` (`CopyAllocation::Process()`, `PinnedAllocation::Process()`, and `ParentAllocation::Process()`).
2. Loop 2 calls the virtual method `Allocation::PostProcess()` (`ParentAllocation::PostProcess()`).

Several HLO transformations across these two loops failed to maintain or propagate `OriginalValue`:
1. While-loop widening in `ParentAllocation::Process()` (Loop 1) and `ParentAllocation::PostProcess()` (Loop 2):
   When `ParentAllocation` passes a buffer from a parent computation into a `while` loop, it widens the `while` loop tuple from N elements to N+1 elements at `new_tuple_index`:
   - `ParentAllocation::Process()` widens the `while` loop inputs by creating a new input tuple (`new_while_operand = TupleUtil::ReplaceTupleWith(...)`) and mutating the shapes of `calling_instruction_` (the `kWhile` instruction), `while_condition->parameter_instruction(0)`, and `while_body->parameter_instruction(0)` in-place. Because the in-place mutated instructions kept their old N-element `OriginalValue` trees while their shapes became (N+1)-tuples, `HloVerifier` failed with shape mismatches. Meanwhile, `new_while_operand` was created with `original_value() == nullptr`.
   - To keep downstream users of the `while` loop valid, `ParentAllocation::Process()` creates `tuple_with_old_shape = TupleUtil::ExtractPrefix(calling_instruction_, new_tuple_index)` and replaces uses of `calling_instruction_` with `tuple_with_old_shape`. `tuple_with_old_shape` and its `GetTupleElement` operands were created with `original_value() == nullptr`, dropping value tracking for all users after the loop.
   - `ParentAllocation::PostProcess()` runs in Loop 2 (after all Loop 1 allocations inside `while_body` have finished) to widen the `while_body` root tuple (`new_while_body_root = TupleUtil::ReplaceTupleWith(added_element, old_body_root, ...)`), which also left `new_while_body_root` with `original_value() == nullptr` and dropped the appended element's `OriginalValue` at `{new_tuple_index}`.
2. Tuple replacement and async copy creation in `CopyAllocation::Process()` and `Allocation::UpdateUses()` (Loop 1):
   - `CopyAllocation::Process()` inserts `copy-start` and `copy-done` instructions to move buffers between default memory (HBM) and alternate memory (VMEM), but left `copy_done_` with `original_value() == nullptr` instead of copying `producing_instruction`'s `OriginalValue`.
   - `CopyAllocation::Process()`, `PinnedAllocation::Process()`, and `ParentAllocation::Process()` all call the helper `Allocation::UpdateUses()` during Loop 1 to rewire consumer instructions to use `producing_instruction`. When a consumer is a `kTuple` instruction (such as `while_body->root_instruction()` or `while_init`), `Allocation::UpdateUses()` calls `TupleUtil::ReplaceTupleWith`, which constructs a brand-new `kTuple` instruction with `original_value() == nullptr`. Consequently, any Loop 1 allocation updating an element of `while_body->root_instruction()` wiped out its `OriginalValue` to `nullptr` before Loop 2 (`ParentAllocation::PostProcess()`) even ran.

What This CL Fixes:
- Add `TupleTree::num_children(ShapeIndexView index = {})` in `tuple_tree.h` to query the number of children of a tuple node directly from the index table.
- Introduce `AppendToTupleOriginalValue(src_tuple, dest_tuple, appended_instr)` in `allocation.cc`, which uses `CopyOriginalValue` from `hlo_original_value_util.h` to map existing tuple elements from `src_tuple` to the widened `dest_tuple` and copies `appended_instr->original_value()->tree()` into the last element (`dest_tuple->shape().tuple_shapes().size() - 1`) via `CopyCompatibleSubtreeFrom`.
- In `ParentAllocation::Process()`, before widening `calling_instruction_` in-place, copy its N-element `OriginalValue` to `tuple_with_old_shape` via `CopyOriginalValue` and propagate subtrees to its `GetTupleElement` operands. Then widen `new_while_operand` with `AppendToTupleOriginalValue` and update `calling_instruction_`, `while_condition` parameter 0, and `while_body` parameter 0 via `AppendToWhileLoopOriginalValue`.
- In `AppendToWhileLoopOriginalValue` (`while_util.cc`), only update `while_body->root_instruction()` if its shape has already been widened to match `while_instr->shape()`, supporting two-phase while-loop widening where `while_body` root widening is deferred to `ParentAllocation::PostProcess()`.
- In `Allocation::AddGetTupleElements()`, propagate the `OriginalValue` subtree from `defining_position().instruction` at `defining_position().index` to the newly created `GetTupleElement` instruction.
- In `ParentAllocation::PostProcess()`, call `AppendToTupleOriginalValue(old_body_root, new_while_body_root, added_element)` so the widened `while_body` root tuple preserves both the body root's `OriginalValue` and the pass-through element's `OriginalValue`.
- In `CopyAllocation::Process()`, propagate `producing_instruction`'s `OriginalValue` to `copy_done_` (and any intermediate bitcast).
- In `Allocation::UpdateUses()`, when `TupleUtil::ReplaceTupleWith` replaces a `kTuple` instruction, clone `tuple_inst`'s `OriginalValue` onto `replacement_instruction` and update `{use.operand_index}` from `producing_instruction->original_value()`.

Clear sharding annotations on entry parameters at the end of GSPMD partitioning.

author: ZMCodi
message:
Add first-class kShuffle instruction and builder API across HLO and platforms.

Introduce `HloOpcode::kShuffle` (`HloShuffleInstruction`), which moves the
elements of its operand around along a set of `dimensions`. A single opcode
covers the whole family of data-movement patterns (rotate, reverse, permute,
...), which keeps the semantic intent available to compiler analysis, layout
assignment, and target-specific lowerings instead of forcing an expansion into
slice and concatenate during graph construction.

The pattern to apply is selected by `xla.ShuffleMode`, a `oneof` pairing each
mode with exactly the attributes that parameterize it, so a mode cannot be
combined with another mode's attributes and adding a mode adds no fields to
`HloInstructionProto`. Switches over `mode()` are exhaustive and have no
`default`, so a new mode does not compile until every consumer has handled it.

Only `rotate` is implemented here. It takes one `shifts` entry per shuffled
dimension and rotates the elements to the left.

Specifically:
*   **HLO IR & Parser**: `HloShuffleInstruction` carries `dimensions` and a
    `ShuffleMode`, with text serialization and parsing. The text form is
    `shuffle(x), dimensions={0,1}, mode=rotate, shifts={2,5}`, where the name of
    a mode is the name of its field in `ShuffleMode`.
*   **Shape Inference & Verifier**: `ShapeInference::InferShuffleShape` and the
    verifier reject duplicate or out-of-range `dimensions`, a missing mode, and
    mode attributes inconsistent with the mode (for `rotate`, `dimensions` and
    `shifts` of unequal size).
*   **XlaBuilder API**: `xla::Shuffle` constructs shuffles from symbolic
    handles. The new `shuffle` utility provides `MakeRotateMode` to build a rotate
    mode and `NormalizeShift` to map an arbitrary shift onto `[0, dim_size)`.
*   **HLO-to-MHLO / StableHLO Translation**: `HloFunctionImporter` imports
    `kShuffle`, lowering each rotated dimension sequentially into
    `stablehlo.slice` and `stablehlo.concatenate`
    (`concat(slice(shift:), slice(0:shift))`).
*   **Pass Integration**: Register `kShuffle` across core compiler passes
    including instruction fusion, layout assignment, and sharding propagation.

author: EusebioDM
message:
Write `ExecutableAndOptionsProto` records uncompressed.

`serialized_executable` is already a snappy-compressed split
`GpuExecutableProto` (see `WriteSplitGpuExecutable`). Compressing the outer
container again saves no space (dropping it adds 0.06% on a 330 MB
executable), but it costs an extra compression pass on write and a full
decompression pass on load.

Riegeli stores the compression type per chunk, so readers don't change and
existing artifacts still load.

Alternative considered: leave the inner proto uncompressed and compress the
outer one instead. That would mean deciding per use case when to skip
compression, which adds logic for little gain, since the outer proto is
small apart from `serialized_executable`.

author: EusebioDM
message:
Parse split-proto merge records from a riegeli::Chain without flattening.

`HandleProtoMergeRecord` read each record into a flat `absl::string_view` and
then called `MergeFromString`. For records larger than a riegeli buffer (e.g.
an HLO module carrying hundreds of MB of constants) the decoded record spans
several blocks, and producing a flat view forces riegeli to copy it into a
contiguous scratch buffer first.

Read the record as a `riegeli::Chain` instead, which shares the decoded
blocks, and parse it with `riegeli::ParseMessage(..., set_merge(true))`,
which consumes the chain directly.

author: akuegel
message:
[XLA:GPU] Require bitcasts to keep bitwidth in CopyFusion

AlgebraicSimplifier can rewrite bitcast-convert instructions into bitcast even
when the element bitwidth changes (when the minor-most dimension is contiguous).
While PriorityFusion and GpuFusible guard against fusing width-changing bitcasts
using hlo_instruction_utils::KeepsBitwidth, CopyFusion previously skipped
through any single-user bitcast without checking its bitwidth.

Fusing a width-changing bitcast and its consuming copy into a producer fusion
breaks the MLIR fusion emitters because GetBitcastMap requires matching element
counts between roots and elemental lowering cannot emit a scalar
mhlo.bitcast_convert across different bitwidths.

Guard kBitcast checks in CopyFusion with hlo_instruction_utils::KeepsBitwidth.

author: bodapatisaikrishna
message:
Fix fatal crash on invalid input rank in GPU linear algebra ops

In GPU linear algebra kernels (DeterminantOpGpu, LogDeterminantOpGpu,
CholeskyOpGpu, MatrixInverseOpGpu, MatrixSolveOpGpu, QrOpGpu), input
rank validation OP_REQUIRES_ASYNC(context, ndims >= 2, ...) was evaluated
after accessing input.dim_size(ndims - 1) or input.dim_size(ndims - 2).

When input had rank < 2 (such as a 0-D scalar), ndims - 1 evaluated to -1
(or ndims - 2 to -2), which triggered a CHECK_GE failure in TensorShapeBase::dim_size
(tensorflow/core/framework/tensor_shape.cc:361: Check failed: d >= 0) and
abruptly killed the entire process with SIGABRT (core dumped) rather than
returning an InvalidArgumentError. On CPU, LinearAlgebraOp validated rank >= 2
before accessing dimensions.

This commit hoists OP_REQUIRES_ASYNC(context, ndims >= 2, ...) (and
OP_REQUIRES_ASYNC(context, rhs.dims() == ndims, ...) in MatrixSolveOpGpu)
before any dim_size indexing across:
- DeterminantOpGpu / LogDeterminantOpGpu (determinant_op.cc)
- CholeskyOpGpu (cholesky_op_gpu.cu.cc)
- MatrixInverseOpGpu (matrix_inverse_op.cc)
- MatrixSolveOpGpu (matrix_solve_op.cc)
- QrOpGpu (qr_op_impl.h)

Matching existing best practices in SVD and LU GPU kernels, and adds unit
tests covering rank < 2 inputs for each op across graph and eager modes.

Fixes #76730

author: akuegel
message:
[XLA:GPU] Clamp per-dimension offsets in dynamic-slice analysis

HLO dynamic-slice and dynamic-update-slice clamp each dimension's start index
i to [0, dim_size[i] - slice_size[i]]. Previously, AnalyzeDynamicSlice and
VerifySliceOffset computed the 1D byte offset directly from unclamped start
indices, relying only on runtime 1D buffer clamping to [0, buffer_size -
slice_size]. When a slice is contiguous because all dimensions major to a
partially-sliced dimension have slice_size == 1, an out-of-bounds offset on a
minor dimension or size-1 dimension could stay within the total buffer bounds
and write or read at the wrong element offset.

Clamp constant offset operands per-dimension in AnalyzeDynamicSlice and
VerifySliceOffset, and for loop-dependent offsets verify that the runtime 1D
buffer clamping matches the per-dimension clamped HLO byte offset on every loop
iteration. Also preserve the sliced operand shape before walking through
bitcasts in DynamicSliceFusion::ResolveParameter so Parameter.shape matches the
slice rank and strides in ComputeSliceOffset.

Fixes #49120

author: mkuperst
message:
[XLA] Disambiguate `kFusion` instructions in `HloCSE` `CseKey` hash based on the fused computation

Previously, `CseKey::AbslHashValue` in `HloCSE` fell into the `default:` branch for `HloOpcode::kFusion`, only hashing the top-level operands, output dimensions, and the fused computation's root opcode. As a result, distinct `kFusion` instructions sharing operands, output shape, and root opcode collided in `HloCSE`'s `representatives` hash table and triggered expensive `HloFusionInstruction::IdenticalSlowPath` (`HloComputation::Equal`) comparisons.

This change factors out `CseKey::HashInstruction` and applies it to the internal instructions of `instruction->fused_instructions_computation()` (in post-order from `root_instruction()`) when hashing a `kFusion` instruction, skipping operand `unique_id()`s for internal instructions so equivalent `kFusion` instructions continue to hash identically while distinct fused computations are disambiguated.

author: vishwakt
message:
Hide only the LLVM C API from libtensorflow_framework

Hiding the llvm:: and mlir:: C++ namespaces broke the build, because
libtensorflow_cc links against those symbols from
libtensorflow_framework. It imports 5,351 of them in the 2.21.0 Linux
wheel, and 3,816 LLVM symbols in a macOS nightly, where the *llvm* and
*LLVM* patterns would have hidden them just the same.

The LLVM C API is different: no other TensorFlow library imports any of
it, on either platform, so hiding it cannot break a link. Keep only
that. On Linux the pattern is LLVM*. On macOS it is _LLVM*, which
carries the Mach-O leading underscore and, unlike *LLVM*, does not also
match C++ names that mention LLVM types.

author: vishwakt
message:
Return 0 from the zero branch of the xlogy/xlog1py/xdivy GPU kernels

The MLIR-generated GPU kernels for these ops, and the TF-dialect
lowering in lower_tf.td that follows the same pattern, select x itself
when x == 0:

  select(x == 0, x, x / y)

That returns -0 for a -0 input. The GPU kernels also flush denormals,
so a subnormal x compares equal to zero and comes back unchanged, which
is how xdivy(1e-40, 1e-40) returns 1e-40 on GPU (#127913). Select zero
instead, as BinaryNoNanPat already does for div_no_nan and as the
tf2xla kernels for these ops already do.

The complex xlog1py kernel also compared x against 1+0j rather than 0,
so xlog1py(1, y) returned 1 for any y, and xlog1py(0, -1) returned nan.
Compare against zero.

The new tests run only on GPU. On CPU these ops run the Eigen functors
in cwise_ops.h, which #127946 covers.

author: retretor
message:
PR #49007: [XLA:GPU] Rewrite FP8 convolutions in all computations of a module

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49007

### 📝 Summary of Changes

`CudnnFusedConvRewriter::RunImpl` iterates over the non-fusion computations of a module and, for each of them, first runs `F8GraphConv`. If `F8GraphConv` rewrote anything, the function returned immediately, so the loop never reached the remaining computations. Any FP8 convolution in a later computation was left as a plain convolution: it got neither the `__cudnn$convForwardGraph` rewrite nor the bias/activation fusions, and the FP8 fallback later demoted it to a legacy non-FP8 `__cudnn$convForward` call.

This change replaces the early `return` with `any_changed |= changed; continue;`. The `continue` keeps the existing behaviour for the rewritten computation (the remaining fusions only match the legacy conv custom calls and do not apply to graph convolutions), and the loop now processes every computation of the module.

### 🎯 Justification

Hit in practice with JAX 0.10.2 on an RTX 5070 (sm_120, CUDA 12.9, cuDNN 9.24). A `jit` for MCTS self-play evaluates an FP8 convolutional network once in the entry computation and again inside a `lax.while_loop` body. Only one of the two copies was rewritten: the compiled HLO contained 20 `__cudnn$convForwardGraph` calls instead of 40, and the other 20 convolutions ran as legacy f32 convolutions. With this change all 40 are FP8 graph convolutions. Which copy loses depends on the computation order, so the workaround was to keep one copy out of FP8 entirely.

Minimal JAX repro (same FP8 convolution in the entry computation and in a while body):

```python
import jax, jax.numpy as jnp
from jax import lax

def conv(x, w):
    return lax.conv_general_dilated(x, w, (1, 1), "SAME",
                                    dimension_numbers=("NHWC", "HWIO", "NHWC"),
                                    preferred_element_type=jnp.float32)

@jax.jit
def f(x, w):
    y0 = conv(x, w) # entry computation
    def body(c):
        i, y = c
        return i + 1, y + conv(y.astype(jnp.float8_e4m3fn), w) # while body
    return lax.while_loop(lambda c: c[0] < 4, body, (0, y0))[1]

x = jnp.ones((1, 6, 6, 128), jnp.float8_e4m3fn)
w = jnp.ones((3, 3, 128, 128), jnp.float8_e4m3fn)
hlo = f.lower(x, w).compile().as_text()
print(hlo.count('custom_call_target="__cudnn$convForwardGraph"'),
      hlo.count('custom_call_target="__cudnn$convForward"'))
```

Before this change (jax-cuda12-pjrt 0.10.2): `1 1` (one graph convolution, one legacy convolution). With this change (plugin rebuilt from the same JAX release with the patched XLA): `2 0`.

### 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

### 🧪 Unit Tests

`CudnnFusedConvRewriterTest.TestConvF8InMultipleComputations` in `cudnn_fused_conv_rewriter_test.cc`. The module has two `conditional` branches, each with an FP8 convolution on a different filter. After `ConvRewriter` and `CudnnFusedConvRewriter` (run with a Hopper compute capability, like the existing F8 tests on pre-FP8 hardware) both branch computations must contain a `__cudnn$convForwardGraph` custom call. Without the fix only the first branch visited is rewritten and the test fails on the second one.

### 🧪 Execution Tests

On FP8-capable GPUs the same test additionally compiles the module through the full pipeline, checks with FileCheck that both convolutions are `__cudnn$convForwardGraph` and no legacy `__cudnn$convForward` remains, and compares the result against the interpreter (`RunAndCompare`, `ErrorSpec{0.15, 0.15}`).

Tested locally on an RTX 5070 (sm_120) with the hermetic CUDA toolchain (cuDNN 9.12): `bazel test //xla/backends/gpu/transforms:cudnn_fused_conv_rewriter_test_nvgpu_any --test_filter='*TestConvF8InMultipleComputations*:*.TestConvF8:*TestConvScaledOutputF8'` passes (the new test runs the full-pipeline branch: `fp8_supported: true`). With the test but without the change in `cudnn_fused_conv_rewriter.cc` the new test fails as intended: `branch_b` keeps the legacy `__cudnn$convForward` custom call.

author: shawnwang18
message:
PR #49155: [XLA:GPU] Preserve async ordering across command buffer boundaries

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49155

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Command buffer conversion can split an async region and, in doing so, lose the ordering between operations queued on the same async stream.

An async start/done pair runs its body on an async stream and joins it back to the main stream at the done. When a region cannot be captured (for example a collective that is disabled for command buffers), the pass still captured any convertible region nested inside it. That moves the nested body into a graph launched on the main stream, where nothing waits for the outer operation that is still running on the async stream.

Notation: `CB{...}` is the set of thunks captured into one command buffer; minimum graph size is 1.

**Example 1, nested pair on the same stream.** `A` and `B` both run on async stream `S`, so `A` must finish before `B` starts. `A` cannot be captured; `B` and the ordinary main-stream command `C` can.

```text
Input:   Start(A); Start(B); C; Done(B); Done(A)
Before:  Start(A); CB{Start(B); C; Done(B)}; Done(A)
After:   Start(A); Start(B); CB{C}; Done(B); Done(A)
```

Before, `B`'s body moves into the graph on the main stream, which has no wait for `A` to complete. After, `B` stays on stream `S` and `A → B` is preserved, while `C` still benefits from capture.

**Example 2, nested pair on a different stream (unchanged).** Same shape, but `B` runs on stream `T`. `B`'s body only ever waited on the main stream, never on `S`, so capturing it loses no ordering. The fix is scoped to the stream of the outstanding operation, so this case keeps the behaviour it has today. The same holds after an unmatched start such as a pipelined recv: only its own stream is affected.

```text
Input:   Start(A on S); Start(B on T); C; Done(B); Done(A)
Before:  Start(A); CB{Start(B); C; Done(B)}; Done(A)
After:   Start(A); CB{Start(B); C; Done(B)}; Done(A)
```

**Example 3, loop body joining an outer operation.** `A` cannot be captured; its done sits inside a loop body together with `C`, which reads `A`'s result. With `WHILE` enabled, the body alone looks convertible.

```text
Input:   Start(A); While{ Done(A); C }
Before:  Start(A); CB{ While{ Done(A); C } }
After:   Start(A); While{ Done(A); CB{C} }
```

Inside a graph the done is a no-op, so before this change `C` could run before `A` finishes. After, the done stays a thunk and only `C` is captured.

This affects partially convertible workloads, such as compute overlapped with collectives that are disabled for command buffers.

Part 1 of 3: #49158 moves LHS dependency construction into the emitter; #48900 then preserves async fork/join ordering inside captured command buffers.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

`command_buffer_async_conversion_test`

PR #46773: Fix unguarded int overflow in ShardingParam and validate on deserialize

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46773

ShardingParam::MinorToMajor::ToDeviceList computed a cumulative axis size product using 32-bit int with no overflow protection, and ShardingParam::verify() computed a dimension-shard product the same unguarded way before using it as a modulo divisor -- if the product wraps to exactly 0, that is a division by zero.\n\nConfirmed via a faithful standalone extraction of both arithmetic patterns, compiled with UBSan+ASan: both overflow with individually plausible input values, and the verify() case produces a real SIGFPE crash when the product wraps to 0.\n\nSeparately, ShardingParam::FromProto never called verify() at all, so a deserialized ShardingParam was never validated before its axis_sizes/dim_shards were used downstream.\n\nThis adds an overflow-safe int64_t accumulation with an explicit range check in verify(), calls verify() from FromProto, and hardens ToDeviceList to fail closed rather than silently propagate a wrapped value.

c015dcb95f89e46df503008a3de0333867b60dd7 by prasanna8585 <65734642+prasanna8585@users.noreply.github.com>:

Fix unguarded int overflow in ShardingParam and validate on deserialize

ShardingParam::MinorToMajor::ToDeviceList computed a cumulative axis
size product using 32-bit int with no overflow protection
(cum_size *= size), and ShardingParam::verify() computed a dimension-
shard product the same unguarded way, then used it as a modulo
divisor (NumDevices() % total_dim_shards_size) -- if the product
wraps to exactly 0, this is a division by zero.

Confirmed via a faithful standalone extraction of both arithmetic
patterns, compiled with UBSan+ASan: both overflow with individually
plausible input values, and the verify() case produces a real SIGFPE
crash when the product wraps to 0.

Separately, ShardingParam::FromProto never called verify() at all, so
a deserialized ShardingParam (e.g. via
xla/python/ifrt_proxy/server/ifrt_backend.cc's handling of
MakeArraysFromHostBufferShards/Assemble requests) was never validated
before its axis_sizes/dim_shards were used downstream.

This adds an overflow-safe int64_t accumulation with an explicit
range check in verify(), calls verify() from FromProto so deserialized
input is actually validated, and hardens ToDeviceList to fail closed
(CHECK) rather than silently propagate a wrapped value into device-
index computation, on the assumption that verify() should have already
caught it upstream.

author: akuegel
message:
[XLA:GPU] Remove side-effecting heroes in DynamicSliceFusionRewriterV2

When `RewriteHero` replaces downstream `dynamic-update-slice` or
`get-tuple-element` instructions rather than the `hero` instruction directly,
`HloComputation::ReplaceInstruction` invokes
`RemoveInstructionAndUnusedOperands` on the downstream instruction. Because
`RemoveInstructionAndUnusedOperands` skips upstream operands that have side
effects (`item->HasSideEffect() && item != instruction`), a side-effecting hero
(such as an FFI custom-call with `custom_call_has_side_effect=true`) and its
sliced operand chain remain alive in the parent computation alongside the newly
created `dynamic_slice_fusion`, causing the side-effecting custom-call to
execute twice.

`RemoveInstructionAndUnusedOperands(hero)` when `hero` has side effects and is
not directly replaced. Also check user counts in `ResolveLeafDus` and
`ResolveNonTupleSlicedResult` (and ensure tuple heroes only have unique GTE
users in `HasSupportedShapes`) so DUS chains are only absorbed when the
hero/GTE has a single user, preventing duplicate heroes when external users

author: sohaibiftikhar
message:
[XLA:GPU]: Allow CUFunction in Record API

Record runs after Prepare -> Initialize.

The following events can happen given 2 GPUs within the same process.
TS1. Thread0 (Host) queues a collective kernel on Gpu0. Asynchronously.
     Gpu0 kernel (device) blocks on GPU1 to also execute the corresponding
     collective on Gpu1.
TS2. Thread0 Records a kernal (with FFI). Calls cuModuleLoad and acquires driver
     mutex. However loading cannot finish until Gpu0 (device) is free. So it
     waits.
TS3. Thread1 which lags a bit behind Thread0 calls cuLaunchKernel but blocks
     because the driver lock was taken during TS2. Collective kernel is never
     launched and GPU0 (TS1) keeps waiting.

To prevent this deadlock we must allow FFI users to load kernels during
preparation. Since not all FFI users can use se::Kernel API for loading we can
allow using a function pointer that was loaded and cached by the FFI user
so cuModuleLoad is not called anymore during the record phase.

Note that this problem only exists for users running single process across multiple GPUs.

author: gauravarun
message:
Reject nouter that doesn't fit in int32 before bounds-check kernel

The bounds-check kernel packs each violation's position into an int32
buffer via GpuAtomicMin. If Index is int64_t and nouter exceeded
INT32_MAX, a position beyond INT32_MAX would truncate to a negative
value when narrowed, which would then be used as a negative pointer
offset when fetching the offending value for the error message.

Guard against this the same way SparseSegmentGradV2Functor already
does for its own nouter/ninner (this file, above): reject the input
with a clear error instead of proceeding with a value that doesn't fit.

author: gauravarun
message:
Address review: guard nouter==0 and avoid full-array D2H copies

- Wrap the GPU validation logic in `if (nouter > 0)` so it no longer
  reads segment_vec[-1] when indices_vec is empty.
- Replace the synchronous full-array copy of `indices`/`segment_ids` to
  the host with a device-side bounds-check kernel that scans both
  arrays in parallel and records only the position of a violation (if
  any) via GpuAtomicMin into a 2-element int32 buffer. Only that tiny
  buffer is transferred back to the host in the common (valid-input)
  case; the actual offending value is fetched with one additional
  single-element copy only when a violation was actually found, to

Addresses review feedback from @dmiltr3.

author: gauravarun
message:
Fix out-of-bounds access in GPU SparseSegment*Grad kernels

SparseSegmentGradFunctor<GPUDevice, ...> (used by SparseSegmentSumGrad,
SparseSegmentMeanGrad, and SparseSegmentSqrtNGrad on GPU) never validated
its `indices` and `segment_ids` inputs before using them to read/write
device memory. The CPU functor bounds-checks every value against the
output-row count and the incoming gradient's row count before using it,
returning InvalidArgumentError on failure; the GPU path had no equivalent
check, so a malformed or out-of-range index caused an out-of-bounds
device read/write, typically surfacing as a fatal
`cudaErrorIllegalAddress` abort that also corrupts the CUDA context for
the rest of the process.

Add the missing validation to the GPU functor by copying the (typically
small) `indices`/`segment_ids` arrays to the host and replicating the
same checks and error messages the CPU functor already uses. Several
existing tests for this were already restricted to `use_gpu=False`
specifically to avoid the crash; this removes that restriction so they
now exercise the fixed GPU path directly.

Fixes #113146.

author: RohithPariki
message:
Fix 1-ULP precision loss and optimize softmax over size-1 axis

When reducing softmax or log_softmax over a dimension of size 1, Eigen's SIMD
vectorized evaluation (AVX2 Packet8f) on batch sizes >= 8 computes reciprocal
approximations (_mm256_rcp_ps + Newton-Raphson) during normalization
(sum of exps = 1.0f). Multiplying by this approximate reciprocal introduces a
1-ULP precision error (yielding 0.99999994f instead of 1.0f).

Furthermore, on GPU, single-class softmax launched two full CUB row reductions
(Max and Sum) and allocated two temporary tensors for size-1 class axes.

This commit introduces a dedicated single-class fast path:
1. In SoftmaxEigenImpl (CPU), directly compute (logits - logits).exp() or
   logits - logits when num_classes == 1, avoiding all class-dimension
   reductions, broadcasts, and reciprocal multiplication while strictly
   preserving IEEE-754 semantics for non-finite inputs.
2. In SoftmaxOpGPU (GPU), dispatch SoftmaxSingleClassKernel when cols == 1,
   eliminating temporary tensor allocations and row reduction kernels.
3. Added regression tests in softmax_op_test.py across SIMD batch boundaries
   and non-finite inputs.

Fixes #116933.

would become local and fail to resolve for anything linking against it.

Too narrow: *llvm* is lowercase and never matched the LLVM C API at all,
whose symbols are spelled LLVM*. Those kept leaking into the dynamic
symbol table, which is the same collision class the change is meant to
close.

prefix for the C API. Verified with lld on the shipped script: llvm::,
mlir:: and LLVM* symbols are dropped while tensorflow::, including
tf_xla_test_use_mlir, and the TF_ C API stay exported. Linking still
succeeds when no pattern matches.

its existing *mlir* entry.

author: beckerhe
message:
Extend the native custom-call emitter context with shapes, kernel arguments and typed attributes

Writing a native custom-call handler requires hand-rolling a large amount of
boilerplate that XLA is in a better position to own, and several of those
hand-rolled pieces are easy to get subtly wrong. This change moves that work
into `NativeCustomCallEmitterContext`, which gains:

-   `GetDeviceDescription()`. Handlers previously had to dig the device
    description out of `GetTargetTopology()->gpu_target_config()`, guarding
    against a target config that, in this code path, is always present.
-   `GetResultShapedSlice()` / `GetOperandShapedSlice()`, which return the
    `ShapedSlice` that thunks actually consume, rather than a bare slice the
    handler then has to pair up with a shape by hand.
-   `CreateKernelArguments()`, which builds the conventional kernel argument
    list. Assembling `emitters::KernelArgument`s by hand leaves `slice_index_`
    uninitialized, skips alignment and aliasing computation, and requires the
    author to set `written` correctly - and `written` drives thunk scheduling,
    so getting it wrong produces races rather than an obvious failure.
    The implementation resolves buffers through `ThunkEmitter`'s allocation
    overrides, which a handler could not have done itself.
-   `GetFfiAttributes()` now returns a typed `ffi::Attributes` instead of an
    `AttributesMap`, so reading an attribute is `attrs.Get<float>("epsilon")`
    rather than two layers of hand-written `std::get_if` on nested variants.
    The demonstrator handler is updated for the new signature.

author: vishwakt
message:
Stop exporting statically linked LLVM and MLIR symbols from libtensorflow_framework

libtensorflow_framework.so is linked with tf_framework_version_script.lds,
which read:

    tensorflow {
      global:
        *;
    };

That declares every symbol global and has no local stanza, so the library
exports its statically linked third-party code as well as its own. Among
those are the LLVM symbols, which then reach the process-wide resolution
scope and collide with any other LLVM loaded into the same process. In the
reported crash an LLVM 15 brought in by llvmlite and numba resolved
llvm::raw_svector_ostream::write_impl against TensorFlow's LLVM 18 and
died on the mismatched layout.

Add a local stanza hiding *llvm* and *mlir*, and add *llvm* to
tf_private_symbols.lds so macOS, which already hides *mlir* through
-unexported_symbols_list, covers the same set.

The change is deliberately narrow. TensorFlow's own symbols stay exported,
because custom op libraries loaded through tf.load_op_library resolve

PR #49146: [XLA:CPU] Replace strict-aliasing-violating type punning with absl::bit_cast

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49146

## [XLA:CPU] Replace strict-aliasing-violating type punning with absl::bit_cast

### Problem
In `onednn_ops_rewriter.cc` and `onednn_op_thunk_test.cc`, converting the IEEE-754 bit representation of `float` epsilon to an `int32_t` config field used pointer-dereference type-punning (`*reinterpret_cast<int32_t*>(&eps)`). Dereferencing an aliased pointer of an incompatible type violates the C++ strict aliasing rule ([basic.lval]), which is undefined behavior and risks miscompilations under aggressive optimization levels.

### Solution
Replace the pointer type-puns with `absl::bit_cast<int32_t>(...)`. This preserves the exact IEEE-754 bit pattern without numeric conversion while adhering strictly to standard aliasing rules.

### Changes
- `xla/service/cpu/onednn_ops_rewriter.cc`: Include `absl/base/casts.h` and use `absl::bit_cast<int32_t>(eps)`.
- `xla/service/cpu/BUILD`: Add `@com_google_absl//absl/base:casts` to `onednn_ops_rewriter` deps.
- `xla/backends/cpu/runtime/onednn/onednn_op_thunk_test.cc`: Include `absl/base/casts.h` and use `absl::bit_cast<int32_t>(epsilon)`.
- `xla/backends/cpu/runtime/onednn/BUILD`: Add `@com_google_absl//absl/base:casts` to `onednn_op_thunk_test` deps.

### Testing
- `git diff --check`: Passed with no whitespace or syntax formatting issues.
- Verified exact 4-file diff matches project include and dependency conventions.

### Risk
Low risk. Behavior-preserving change that preserves identical bit-level values while removing undefined behavior.

author: kodlan
message:
PR #47282: [XLA:TSL] Fix silent truncation of ZlibOutputBuffer appends larger than 4 GiB

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47282

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`ZlibOutputBuffer::Append` passes data that does not fit in the staging buffer directly to zlib by assigning the `size_t` byte count to `z_stream::avail_in`, which is zlib's 32-bit `uInt`. A single `Append` of 4 GiB or more is truncated to `size % 2^32` bytes: the write reports OK, `Close()` produces a well-formed gzip stream, and everything past the truncated count is silently lost.

This change chunks the direct-deflate path so zlib is fed at most `uInt` max bytes per round, and adds a round-trip regression test that appends 4 GiB + 1 MiB in one call. The test lives in its own `size = "large"` target (`zlib_buffers_large_append_test`) because it needs ~4 GiB of memory for the input string; the existing `zlib_buffers_test` stays `small`.

This completes the fix started in 783463ddeb, which addressed the size comparisons but not the `avail_in` assignment (see the reporter's follow-up in the issue).

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #28159: profiling a large workload makes `jax.profiler.stop_trace()` write the whole Chrome-trace JSON through one `Append` call in `WriteGzippedDataToFile` (`xla/tsl/profiler/rpc/client/save_profile.cc`); above 4 GiB the resulting `<host>.trace.json.gz` decompresses to a truncated JSON document. Fixing `Append` itself (rather than chunking in `save_profile.cc`) also covers the other users of this class (`record_writer`, `xla/service/dump.cc`).

Reproduced at HEAD: appending 2^32 + 2^20 bytes produced a file that decompresses to exactly 2^20 bytes (`size % 2^32`).

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

- New target `//xla/tsl/lib/io:zlib_buffers_large_append_test` (`size = "large"`, ~4 GiB peak RSS, 8 s at `Z_BEST_SPEED`): single 4 GiB + 1 MiB `Append`, round-tripped through `ZlibInputStream` with full content verification and an end-of-stream check. Fails before this change (first read hits `OUT_OF_RANGE: EOF reached` - the file decompresses to exactly `size % 2^32` = 1 MiB), passes after.
- All 13 test targets in `//xla/tsl/lib/io/...` pass with the change.
- For appends below 4 GiB the loop runs exactly one iteration with the same zlib call sequence as before, so existing behavior is unchanged (covered by the existing round-trip tests, which exercise the direct-deflate branch with data larger than the staging buffer).

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

Not applicable (host-side I/O library; no device execution involved).

author: chsigg
message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix Triton codegen for scans with a tiled scan dimension.

When the scan dimension is tiled, the scan is emitted inside an `scf.for` loop
and the carry of each tile becomes the init of the next one. That carry never
compiled:

*   `LowerScan::ExtractCarries` extracted the last element along the scan
    dimension with a `tensor.extract_slice`, which has no lowering to the
    TritonGPU dialect.
*   For 1D scans, the rank-reduced carry and therefore the `scf.for` `iter_arg`
    was a rank-zero tensor, which is illegal in TritonGPU
    (`BlockedEncodingAttr::get` asserts rank >= 1).

Instead of rank-reducing the scan dimension, the inits and carries of
`xtile.scan` now keep it as a unit dimension and have the same rank as the scan
inputs and outputs. Carries are therefore never rank-zero, and the init is
broadcast over the tile with a `tt.broadcast`, both without any reshapes. A new
`xtile.scan` verifier enforces this.

`tt.scan` does not return the final carry, so it has to be extracted from the
scan output. Gathering it with a `tt.gather` would write the entire tile to
shared memory. Instead, mask all other elements to zero and select the
remaining one with an `or` reduction over the bitcast integer values, which is
exact because zero is the neutral element of `or`. This is the established
pattern for tiled Triton scans, see `triton_helpers.select_one` in PyTorch
inductor and proger/accelerated-scan. It reduces the shared memory of the added
tiled scan tests from 1024 to 16 bytes (1D) and from 4096 to 128 bytes (2D),
and lowers to a single `redux.sync.or.b32` per warp on sm_80 and later.

Also fix `GetDimsToSqueeze`, which keeps one unit dimension by popping the last
entry when all dimensions have size one. For a rank-zero tensor there is no
entry to pop and it read past the end of the `SmallVector`.

None of this was caught because the only scan test reaching the emitter tiled
the whole scan into a single tile, so the carry was dead and got eliminated.
Add tests that check the emitted IR and the numerics of tiled scans.

author: beckerhe
message:
Share custom kernel binaries between kernel loader specs.

`KernelReuseCache` deduplicates kernel *compilation*, but every consumer deep
copies the compiled binary out of the cache entry, because
`CreateOwnedCubinCustomKernel` takes the CUBIN by value. A module that invokes
the same kernel N times therefore keeps N copies of its CUBIN in memory, and the
Triton fusion emitter copies it twice, because `TritonFusion::EmitResult` holds
the cache entry by value.

Add reference counted `SharedCudaCubinInMemory` and `SharedCudaPtxInMemory`
payloads to `se::KernelLoaderSpec`, keep `KernelReuseCache::Entry::binary` in a
`std::shared_ptr`, and switch the three cached emitter call sites to the new
`CreateSharedCubinCustomKernel` factory. `KernelLoaderSpec` remains a value type
and its accessors keep handing out non-owning views, so every reader - including
`ToProto` - is unaffected. The two emitters that have no cache keep the owning
factory, since they have nothing to share with.

The serialized representation is unchanged; this only removes redundant copies
in memory. Deduplicating the serialized form follows in a later change.

author: Phoebus-Liu
message:
Fix tnp.sinc gradient at zero

`tf.experimental.numpy.sinc` evaluates `sin(pi_x) / pi_x` and selects away
from it at `x == 0` with `where`. That discarded branch is 0/0 there, and
`where` still propagates its gradient (0 * nan is nan), so the gradient at
zero came out as `nan` instead of `0`.

Substituting 1 for the denominator in the discarded branch leaves the
forward values bit-for-bit identical (the branch is never selected) while
making it finite, so its contribution is scaled to exactly 0.

Adds a regression test that fails before the change and passes after.

message:
Copy removal: count a view's readers as uses of the viewed value

CopyInsertion takes an optional view color. A view colored value is an
address stand in that owns no storage and aliases its operand 0's buffer.
Copy removal then counts the transitive readers of a value's view colored
users as uses of that value, so no producer is merged into the viewed
buffer between a view and its readers. Backends without views are
unchanged.

author: soreavis
message:
JSON - support ${workspaceFolder} in json.schemas fileMatch patterns (#326706)

* JSON - support ${workspaceFolder} in json.schemas fileMatch patterns

A fileMatch pattern has no way to target files in the workspace folder
root only: patterns are matched against the full document uri with an
implicit '**/' prefix, so `*.json` matches at every depth and a leading
`/` is redundant.

Expand a leading `${workspaceFolder}` (also after a `!` exclusion
prefix) to the workspace folder uri when collecting json.schemas
settings, in the two scopes with an unambiguous folder: workspace
folder settings in a multi-root workspace and workspace settings of a
single folder workspace. The expanded pattern is absolute, so the
implicit '**/' prefix no longer widens it and
`${workspaceFolder}/*.json` matches in the folder root only. The
server API stays unchanged.

Fixes #44135

* JSON - escape glob metacharacters when expanding ${workspaceFolder}

The service's glob has no escape syntax, so a folder name containing a
glob metacharacter altered the meaning of the expanded pattern: names
with brackets or braces made it match nothing and a '*' made it match
too much. Since the glob passes a backslash and alphanumerics through
to the resulting regular expression verbatim, encoding the folder
string's metacharacters as regex hex escapes makes them match
literally.

Also drop the query and fragment from the folder uri, mirroring what
the server does to document uris before matching.

* JSON - use startsWith to detect the ${workspaceFolder} prefix

* JSON - expand ${workspaceFolder} to the folder path

* JSON - move the glob escaping to a strings util

* JSON - percent-encode # and ? when expanding ${workspaceFolder}

defaulting to `never` and rolled out through experimentation (legacy `true` and

agentHost: Keep remote hosts alive while agents are running (#338392)

* agentHost: Keep remote hosts alive while agents are running

The --idle-timeout supervisor on remote agent hosts only counted connected clients, so it shut the agent host down 300s after the last client disconnected, even while a turn was still running. It now also counts the agent host server process as activity. The server already stays up while a turn is running and exits on its own once idle. Server exit is detected from the process itself rather than from its output pipes closing.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: Avoid signaling a reused PID when killing the server

The task that owns the server process reaps it before the running-server state is cleared, so kill_running_server could run kill_tree on a PID the OS had already reassigned. Kill requests now go through that task, which either reaps a process that exited on its own or kills it before reaping.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: Let run_server own the server process until it exits

start_server already spawns run_server and awaits only its readiness barrier, so run_server now waits for the process to exit or a kill request itself instead of handing the process to a second task. This leaves one owner for the process through startup, kill, and reap. The output reader stays a separate task because descendants can keep the pipes open after the server exits.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

author: roblourens
message:
agentHost: settle in-flight turns when a remote connection is replaced (#338211)

* agentHost: settle in-flight turns when a remote connection is replaced

A remote Agent Host session could reopen showing a stale, in-progress conversation while the session list showed it idle (#336638). When a remote connection is replaced (host restart, or reconnect with a new clientId), the old AgentHostSessionHandler is disposed. A turn it was awaiting never settled, because its observer read the dead connection's state. The in-progress request kept the ChatModel alive, and loadRemoteSession reused that stale model instead of resolving the current state from the new connection.

- Track turns awaited by _invokeAgent/_handleTurn/_handleResumedTurn and settle them when the handler is disposed, without dispatching turnCancelled to the host.
- Complete an AgentHostChatSession's active turn when it is disposed, for restored and server-initiated streamed turns.
- Stop an invocation that is still preparing from creating a session, claiming an active client, or dispatching its turn on a handler that is being disposed.
- Keep treating a model's queue as server-managed after its session contribution is unregistered, so completing the stale turn does not send the host's queued messages from the client.

Fixes #336638

(Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: stop abandoned invocations at the remaining disposal windows

Address review feedback on #338211. An invocation on a handler disposed during these waits could still act on the replaced connection or hang:

- Check for abandonment after resolving trust folders, before a workspace-trust prompt.
- Check again after interactive authentication, before retrying createSession.
- Settle the wait for the new session's subscription to hydrate from the handler's lifetime. Disposing a subscription fires neither onDidChange nor onDidError, so the wait could hang and keep the stale model in progress.

(Written by Copilot)

automations: fix: prevent timestamp from being pushed to the end for failed items

The automation history list rendered failed items with the timestamp
pushed to the far right instead of appearing inline as

`.session-description` shared a `flex: 1` rule with `.session-title`.

description element (the function returns undefined), and
InProgress/NeedsInput items hide the whole details row, so Failed was
the only status exposing the bug.

Give `.session-description` its own rule without `flex: 1` so it sizes
to its content instead of expanding to push the timestamp away.

author: dmitrivMS
message:
copilot: fix shell argument injection in generated commit messages (#337547)

* Fix shell argument injection in generated commit messages

The commit-message sanitizer escaped `"` before `\`, so the second replace
re-escaped the backslash the first one had just added and turned `"` into
`\\"`. Inside a double-quoted shell string that reads as an escaped backslash
followed by a closing quote, ending the `-m` argument early and leaving the
rest of the message to be parsed as separate shell tokens. Backticks were not
escaped at all, so a message containing `cmd` in backticks still triggered
command substitution.

Quote the message with single quotes instead, which suppress expansion and
substitution outright rather than depending on every metacharacter being
escaped individually. Quoting is shell-aware because `'` is not a quote
character in cmd.exe and PowerShell escapes an embedded `'` by doubling it
rather than with the POSIX `'\''` idiom. This also fixes the previous `\`
doubling silently corrupting backslashes under PowerShell.

The helper lives in its own module so it is covered by the fast unit suite
and can be reused by the other terminal sendText call sites.

Fixes #316995
Fixes #316996

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Harden commit-message quoting per shell, else use the commit box

The first fix still let a generated message break out of its quoted
argument in several shells. Because sendText turns every line break into an
Enter key press, a breakout in a multi-line message ran without the user
pressing Enter.

- PowerShell also ends a single-quoted string at the typographic single
  quotes U+2018, U+2019, U+201A and U+201B, which are common in generated
  text.
- Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not escape an embedded double quote when it
  builds git's command line, so the quote split the argument. PowerShell 5.1
  and 7 both report the shell as pwsh, so a double quote is refused.
- fish treats \' and \\ as escapes inside single quotes, so a backslash
  defeated the POSIX '\'' idiom.
- nu has no escape for a single quote. cmd.exe expands %VAR% inside double
  quotes and runs each line as soon as it is entered. csh expands ! inside
  single quotes and cannot continue them onto a new line.

Typed control characters are also commands to the shell's line editor; for
example, a Backspace can erase the opening quote. A message containing one
is refused for every shell.

quoteShellArgument now uses an allowlist of shells whose quoting rules are
known, and returns undefined when a value cannot be quoted safely. The

author: lszomoru
message:
Engineering - decompose macOS build stage (#338655)

* Engineering - decompose macOS stage

Split the macOS product build into Compile, Test and Sign jobs so failed jobs can be retried without repeating successful work. Compile publishes the unpacked builds, Test applies the local entitlement signature and runs the tests with retry checkpoints, and Sign mixes in the CLI, packages, signs, notarizes and publishes the final artifacts. The arm64 test job gates publishing of the arm64 and universal artifacts.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - split macOS stage per architecture

Move the macOS x64, arm64 and universal product builds into dedicated macOSX64, macOSARM64 and macOSUniversal stages, following the Windows and Linux layout. The existing macOS stage continues to hold the CI test jobs. Rename the CLI job to macOS_<arch>_CLI / "macOS (ARCH) - CLI" to match the other platforms, and update publish.ts and the artifact sanity tests to the new stage names.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - publish unsigned macOS client from the Compile job

The macOS (UNIVERSAL) job only waits 60 minutes for the unsigned x64 and arm64 clients. Publishing them from the Sign job delayed them until the Compile and CLI jobs had completed and a new agent had set up and extracted the compilation artifact, so the universal job timed out. Mix in the CLI and publish the unsigned client from the Compile job again, at the same point as before the job split. The compilation artifact now contains the CLI, so the Test and Sign jobs only depend on the Compile job.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - fix Linux CLI producer name in package steps

The Linux CLI job was renamed to "Linux (ARCH) - CLI", so the CLI artifact wait no longer recognized its producer and could not short circuit when the CLI job failed.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - align macOS UNIVERSAL stage display name

Use upper case for the architecture, matching the other product build stages.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - download remote Node.js in macOS test job

The remote integration tests run 'gulp node', which downloads the Node.js runtime from Azure Artifacts unless it is already cached. The macOS test job no longer builds the server, so the runtime is not cached and the download fails without authentication. Download it with Azure Artifacts authentication before running the tests, as the Linux test job does.

author: anthonykim1
message:
Retain full Codex shell output across chat reloads (#337390)

* Retain full Codex command output with its chat session

Store command output longer than 20,000 characters in the owning chat's
session database and publish a 2,000-character preview with a non-PTY
terminal resource, so "Open Full Output" works for Codex the same way it
does for Copilot. Restored chats get the same resource back when the
database has the output; other output keeps its restored text.

Use the Codex item id as the command's tool call id, live and on replay,
so the resource survives reloads. A sandbox pre-flight coalesced with its
re-run keeps the pre-flight's id on replay too, matching live.

The completion is still published synchronously and no terminal is kept
alive: subscribers get exited terminal state rebuilt from the database,
whose queued write is ordered ahead of later reads. Reverting or rolling
back turns removes the output retained for their commands.

* Keep Codex command output inline up to the shell output limit

Codex reports a command's complete output, so only retain output that is
longer than the SHELL_COMMAND_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES characters the agent host
already surfaces for shell output, instead of the workbench's model-facing
20,000-character limit. Output at or below that size renders exactly as it
did before.

When output is retained, keep its end inline as the preview rather than its
first 2,000 characters. The terminal card shows the end of the output, so the
card keeps showing what it showed before, and Open Full Output serves the rest.

* Unwrap PowerShell command executions in Codex chat

Treat PowerShell and pwsh -Command wrappers like the existing Bash and zsh
-c wrappers when rendering Codex command executions. Retained output remains
shell-neutral; this keeps Windows command rows and restored transcripts on the
same display path as POSIX shells.

* Show the beginning of retained Codex command output

Keep the first 80,000 characters as the inline preview when Codex output is
retained, matching Claude's first-chunk presentation. Below-limit output and
the complete stored terminal resource remain unchanged.

* Keep the beginning visible in retained Codex previews

Build a compact preview from the first three logical output lines and shorten
very long lines. This keeps the beginning visible in the terminal card's fixed
viewport while the complete output remains available through Open Full Output.

* Keep retained Codex previews as a raw prefix

Use the first 400 output characters exactly as emitted, without synthesizing
ellipsis markers or rewriting lines. The bounded prefix remains visible in the
terminal card while Open Full Output serves the complete stored result.

* Retain Codex output recovered at turn completion

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337390#discussion_r4092208196.
Queue retained-output storage before recovered command completions are mapped
from turn/completed, preserving the normal item/completed ordering.

* Restore retained Codex output during history refresh

Addresses review thread https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/337390#discussion_r4092208234.
Enrich changed replayed turns from the session database before publishing
incremental history replacements, with a staleness guard after the async read.

* Keep recovered Codex subagent output inline

Preserve the PR's existing subagent exclusion while retaining parent command
output recovered from turn/completed. Share the recovery predicate with the
storage path and cover both parent and subagent outcomes.

* Fix Codex retained-output regression test types

Use the current generated protocol item shapes and narrow retained terminal
content before reading its resource. This keeps the Copilot review regressions
type-safe without changing production behavior.

* Codex: preserve full output when retention fails

Addresses review comment 4098872570. Wait for output storage before publishing completion, retain inline output on failure, and preserve per-chat progress order.

* Codex: skip encoding output above the retention limit

Addresses review comment 4098872582. Reject oversized strings before allocating a UTF-8 copy, and retain the exact byte check for multibyte output.

* Codex: define the inline output limit in characters

Addresses review comment 4098872591. Decouple the 80,000-code-unit Codex transcript limit from the shared shell tool byte limit and cover Unicode boundaries.

* Codex: preserve shell flags when coalescing commands

Addresses review comment 4098872600. Compare raw invocations for live and replay pre-flight identity while keeping unwrapped scripts for display and restriction checks.

* Codex: share the command completion recovery predicate

Addresses review comment 4098872608. Keep recovered-output retention and completion mapping on the same eligibility check.

* Codex: restore retained output independently of replay length

Addresses review comment 4098872611. Look up retained rows by tool-call id and recover the preview from storage when native history is short or empty.

author: lszomoru
message:
Engineering - split Windows stage into multiple stages/jobs (#338404)

* Engineering - Reuse Windows compilation outputs on job retries

Windows product build jobs can fail for reasons unrelated to compilation
(flaky tests, codesigning dependencies), and retrying them used to compile
everything again. The x64 and arm64 jobs now publish their compilation
outputs as a pipeline artifact before the CLI is added and codesigning
runs. On a retry, the job restores that artifact and skips all
compilation steps.

A temporary step fails the first job attempt after the artifact is
published so that the retry path can be validated. It must be removed
before merging.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - Split Windows product build into compile, test and sign jobs

Retrying a failed Windows product build job used to repeat all of its work,
even when only a flaky test or an external code signing dependency failed.
The Windows x64 and arm64 product jobs are now split into three jobs:

- Compile: compiles the client, server and web server builds and publishes
  them as the compilation_win32_<arch> pipeline artifact.
- Test (x64 only): downloads the compilation artifact and runs the tests.
- Sign: downloads the compilation artifact, adds the CLI, code signs and
  packages the builds, and publishes the product artifacts.

The test and sign jobs both depend on the compile job and run in parallel,
so retrying a failed job never repeats the work of a job that succeeded.
This replaces the in-job reuse of the compilation outputs.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - Sign the Windows CLI in the Windows sign job

The Windows CLI job built the CLI and signed it, while the Windows sign job
polled for the unsigned CLI and signed the same executable again as part of
the client build. A code signing failure in the CLI job also meant building
the CLI again on retry.

The CLI job now only builds the CLI and publishes the unsigned artifact. The
Windows sign job depends on both the compile and the CLI jobs instead of
polling for the CLI artifact, signs the CLI once as part of the client build,
and publishes the standalone vscode_cli_win32_<arch>_cli artifact from that
signed executable.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - Skip passed test tasks when retrying the Windows x64 test job

Retrying the Windows x64 test job ran every test task again, even when only
one of them failed. Each test task now records a checkpoint artifact as soon
as it passes, and retries of the job skip the test tasks that already passed
in an earlier attempt of the same pipeline run. The WSL Dev Container setup is
skipped together with the Electron smoke tests it serves.

This ports the test checkpoints from #334926 to the Windows x64 test job. The
VSCODE_SKIP_SUCCESSFUL_TEST_TASKS queue parameter (default true) enables them;
all other jobs are unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Engineering - Always skip passed Windows test tasks and align Windows job names

- Remove the VSCODE_SKIP_SUCCESSFUL_TEST_TASKS parameter: the Windows test
  steps always record checkpoints and skip the test tasks that already passed
  in an earlier attempt of the job. This also applies to the Windows CI test
  jobs, which share the same test steps. All test tasks, including the unit
  tests, now use the run-test-with-checkpoint template.
- Rename the Windows CLI job to Windows_<arch>_CLI ("Windows (<ARCH>) - CLI")
